book.old: t('Meet the royal family of the keys. The King sings low, the Queen sings high, and Clara lives between them on middle C. This chapter writes their notes down, so your eyes can read what your hands play.', '건반의 왕실 가족을 만나요. 왕은 낮은 목소리로, 여왕은 높은 목소리로 노래하고, 클라라는 그 사이 가운데 도에 살아요. 이 챕터에서는 이들의 음을 종이에 써요, 손이 치는 것을 눈으로 읽을 수 있게요.')
book.new: t('Meet the royal family of the keys. The King sings low, the Queen sings high. Clara lives between them, on middle C. Now we read their notes on paper.', '건반의 왕실 가족을 만나요. 왕은 낮은 목소리, 여왕은 높은 목소리로 노래해요. 클라라는 그 사이 가운데 도에 살아요. 이제 이들의 음을 종이에서 읽어요.')

book.old: <>오선에는 줄 다섯 개와 칸 네 개가 있어요. 아래에서부터 세요: 1번 줄이 가장 낮고 5번 줄이 가장 높아요; 1번 칸은 1번 줄 바로 위예요. 음표는 모두 줄 위에 있거나(줄이 음표 한가운데를 꿰뚫어요, 꼬치처럼) 칸 안에 있어요: 칸을 꽉 채워서 위아래 줄에 닿아요, 샌드위치 속처럼.
book.new: <>오선에는 줄 다섯 개와 칸 네 개가 있어요. 아래에서부터 세요: 1번 줄이 가장 낮고, 1번 칸은 그 바로 위예요. 줄 위 음표는 줄이 가운데를 꿰뚫어요, 꼬치처럼. 칸 안 음표는 위아래 줄에 닿아요, 샌드위치 속처럼.

book.old: <>The staff has five lines and four spaces. Count them from the bottom: line 1 is the lowest, line 5 the highest; space 1 sits just above line 1. Every note lives either on a line (the line runs straight through its middle, like a skewer) or in a space: it fills the space and touches the line above and the line below, like a sandwich filling.
book.new: <>The staff has five lines and four spaces. Count from the bottom: line 1 is the lowest, space 1 just above it. On a line, the line runs through the note, like a skewer. In a space, the note touches both lines, like a sandwich filling.

book.old: <>오선은 건반의 지도예요. 오선에서 위에 있는 음은 높은 소리: 피아노에서 오른쪽, 하늘 위 새 쪽이에요. 아래는 왼쪽, 바다 아래 거북이 쪽이에요. 줄에서 바로 위 칸으로 가면 한 걸음: 다음 글자, 다음 흰건반. 줄에서 다음 줄로(칸에서 다음 칸으로) 가면 건너뛰기: {bkChapterNo('note-names')}챕터의 그 건너뛰기, 글자 하나를 넘어가요.
book.new: <>오선은 건반의 지도예요. 오선에서 위는 높은 소리: 오른쪽, 하늘 위 새 쪽. 아래는 왼쪽, 바다 아래 거북이 쪽. 줄에서 바로 다음 칸은 한 걸음: 다음 글자, 다음 흰건반. 줄에서 다음 줄, 칸에서 다음 칸은 건너뛰기: {bkChapterNo('note-names')}챕터처럼 글자 하나를 넘어가요.

book.old: <>The staff is a map of the keys. A note higher on the staff sounds higher: it is further to the right on the piano, up towards the bird; lower on the staff is further left, down towards the turtle. From a line to the very next space is a step: the next letter, the next white key. From a line to the next line, or a space to the next space, is a skip: the same skip as in Chapter {bkChapterNo('note-names')}, one letter jumped over.
book.new: <>The staff is a map of the keys. Higher on the staff is higher on the piano: to the right, up towards the bird. Lower is to the left, down towards the turtle. Line to the next space is a step: the next letter, the next white key. Line to the next line, or space to the next space, is a skip: one letter jumped over, as in Chapter {bkChapterNo('note-names')}.

book.old: <>Start on any white key and play the picture's steps: up to the top of the hill and back down, the next key each time.
book.new: <>Start on any white key and play the picture's steps: up to the top and back down, the next key each time.

book.old: <>이 꼬불꼬불한 기호가 높은음자리표예요. 아주 옛날에는 그냥 글자 G였어요. 소용돌이가 아래에서 둘째 줄을 감싸는데, 그 줄이 여왕의 집이에요: 그 줄 위의 음은 모두 G. 여왕은 높은 목소리로 노래하고, 보통 오른손이 읽어요. 클라라(가운데 도)에서 여왕의 G까지는 딱 다섯 음: C D E F G, 클라라는 오선 아래 작은 사다리 발판 위, D는 1번 줄 바로 아래, E는 1번 줄, F는 1번 칸, G는 여왕의 줄.
book.new: <>높은음자리표는 글자 G에서 시작했어요. 소용돌이가 감싸는 둘째 줄이 여왕의 집: 그 줄의 음은 모두 G예요. 여왕은 높은 목소리로 노래하고, 보통 오른손이 읽어요. 클라라(가운데 도)에서 여왕의 G까지 다섯 음: C D E F G. C는 클라라의 작은 사다리 발판, D는 1번 줄 아래, E는 1번 줄, F는 1번 칸, G는 여왕의 줄.

book.old: <>This curly sign is the treble clef. Long ago it was simply a letter G. Its curl wraps round the second line from the bottom, and that line is the Queen's house: every note on it is G. The Queen sings high, and usually the right hand reads her staff. From Clara (middle C) up to the Queen's G is exactly five notes: C D E F G. Clara on her little ladder under the staff, D just under line 1, E on line 1, F in space 1, G on the Queen's line.
book.new: <>The treble clef began as a letter G. Its curl wraps the second line, the Queen's house: every note on it is G. The Queen sings high. The right hand usually reads her staff. Clara (middle C) to the Queen's G is five notes: C D E F G. C on Clara's little ladder, D under line 1, E on line 1, F in space 1, G on the Queen's line.

book.old: <>오른손으로 가운데 도에서 G까지 걸어 올라가요: C D E F G, 오선의 그림을 보면서, 글자를 말하면서.
book.new: <>오른손으로 가운데 도에서 G까지 올라가요: C D E F G. 오선을 읽으며 글자를 말해요.

book.old: <>With your right hand, walk up from middle C to G: C D E F G, looking at the staff picture, saying the letters.
book.new: <>Right hand, from middle C up to G: C D E F G. Read the staff and say each letter.

book.old: <>여왕의 소용돌이 그리기: 높은음자리표는 G 줄에서 시작해 밖으로 감아 나가요. 여왕의 집에서 출발! (워크북에 따라 그리는 쪽이 있어요.)
book.new: <>여왕의 소용돌이 그리기: 여왕의 집 G 줄에서 시작해 밖으로 감아 나가요. 워크북에 따라 그리는 쪽이 있어요.

book.old: <>Draw the Queen's curl: a treble clef starts on the G line and spirals out. It begins at the Queen's house! (The Workbook has one to trace.)
book.new: <>Draw the Queen's curl: start on the G line, her house, and spiral out. The Workbook has one to trace.

book.old: <>이 기호는 낮은음자리표예요. 글자 F에서 시작했어요. 왕의 집은 아래에서 넷째 줄이고, 음자리표의 두 점이 경비병이에요: 하나는 왕의 줄 바로 위, 하나는 바로 아래. 두 경비병 사이의 줄이 F예요. 왕은 낮은 목소리로 노래하고, 보통 왼손이 읽어요. 왕의 F에서 클라라까지도 딱 다섯 음: F G A B C, F는 왕의 줄, G는 그 위 칸, A는 맨 윗줄, B는 그 위, C는 오선 위 작은 사다리 발판의 클라라.
book.new: <>낮은음자리표는 글자 F에서 시작했어요. 두 점은 왕의 경비병, 넷째 줄 바로 위와 바로 아래에 있어요. 그 줄이 왕의 집: 그 줄의 음은 모두 F예요. 왕은 낮은 목소리로 노래하고, 보통 왼손이 읽어요. 왕의 F에서 클라라까지도 다섯 음: F G A B C. F는 왕의 줄, G는 그 위 칸, A는 맨 윗줄, B는 그 위, C는 클라라의 작은 사다리 발판.

book.old: <>This sign is the bass clef. It began as a letter F. The King's house is the fourth line from the bottom, and the clef's two dots are his guards, one just above his line and one just below. The line between the guards is F. The King sings low, and usually the left hand reads his staff. From the King's F up to Clara is five notes too: F G A B C. F on the King's line, G in the space above, A on the top line, B just over it, and Clara on her little ladder above the staff.
book.new: <>The bass clef began as a letter F. Its two dots are the King's guards, just above and below the fourth line. That line is the King's house: every note on it is F. The King sings low. The left hand usually reads his staff. The King's F to Clara is five notes too: F G A B C. F on the King's line, G in the space above, A on the top line, B over it, C on Clara's little ladder.

book.old: <>왕의 경비병 그리기: 낮은음자리표는 F 줄 위의 점에서 시작해 동그랗게 내려가요. 그리고 F 줄 위아래에 경비병 두 점! (워크북에 따라 그리는 쪽이 있어요.)
book.new: <>왕의 경비병 그리기: F 줄 위의 점에서 시작해 동그랗게 내려가요. 그다음 F 줄 위아래에 경비병 두 점. 워크북에 따라 그리는 쪽이 있어요.

book.old: <>Draw the King's guards: a bass clef starts with a dot on the F line and curls down. Then the two guards, one above the F line and one below. (The Workbook has one to trace.)
book.new: <>Draw the King's guards: start with a dot on the F line and curl down. Then the two guards, above and below the F line. The Workbook has one to trace.

book.old: <>왼손으로 가운데 도에서 F까지 걸어 내려가요: C B A G F. 그다음 F에서 다시 올라와요: F G A B C.
book.new: <>왼손으로 가운데 도에서 F까지 내려가요: C B A G F. 그다음 다시 올라와요: F G A B C.

book.old: <>With your left hand, walk down from middle C to F: C B A G F. Then back up from F: F G A B C.
book.new: <>Left hand, from middle C down to F: C B A G F. Then back up: F G A B C.

book.old: <>여왕의 오선을 위에, 왕의 오선을 아래에 두고 앞에서 선으로 묶으면 큰보표예요, 손마다 오선 하나씩. 두 궁전 사이, 가운데 도에 클라라가 살아요: 2챕터의 땅이에요. 클라라는 한 명이고, 음도 자기만의 작은 사다리 발판 하나뿐이에요. 여왕네 갈 때는 여왕의 오선 바로 아래에 쓰고, 왕네 갈 때는 왕의 오선 바로 위에 써요. 종이에서는 두 자리처럼 보여도 피아노에서는 같은 건반이에요.
book.new: <>여왕의 오선을 위에, 왕의 오선을 아래에 두고 앞에서 선으로 묶으면 큰보표예요, 손마다 오선 하나씩. 두 궁전 사이 가운데 도에 클라라가 살아요: 2챕터의 땅. 클라라는 한 명, 작은 사다리 발판도 하나. 여왕네 갈 때는 여왕의 오선 바로 아래, 왕네 갈 때는 왕의 오선 바로 위에 써요. 종이에서는 두 자리, 피아노에서는 같은 건반.

book.old: <>Put the Queen's staff on top and the King's underneath, joined by a line at the start: that is the grand staff, one staff for each hand. Between the two palaces, on middle C, lives Clara: the ground from Chapter 2. There is one Clara, and she has one little ladder of her own. Visiting the Queen, her note is written just under the Queen's staff; visiting the King, just over his. Two places on paper, the same key on the piano.
book.new: <>The Queen's staff on top, the King's below, joined by a line at the start: the grand staff, one staff per hand. Clara lives between the palaces, on middle C: the ground from Chapter 2. One Clara, one little ladder of her own. Visiting the Queen, write her just under the Queen's staff. Visiting the King, just over his. Two places on paper, the same key on the piano.

book.old: <>어느 궁전? 누가 클라라의 음을 위 오선 아래에 쓰거나 아래 오선 위에 써요: 위에 붙어도 아래에 붙어도 같은 건반이에요. 매번 가운데 도를 쳐요. 오른손으로도, 왼손으로도.
book.new: <>어느 궁전? 누가 클라라의 음을 위 오선 아래나 아래 오선 위에 써요. 매번 가운데 도를 쳐요, 오른손으로도 왼손으로도: 같은 건반.

book.old: <>Which palace? Someone writes Clara's note under the top staff or over the bottom one: attached up or attached down, it is the same key. Play middle C each time, with the right hand and with the left.
book.new: <>Which palace? Someone writes Clara's note under the top staff or over the bottom one. Play middle C each time, with the right hand and with the left: the same key.

guide.old: Music is written on a staff: five lines and the four spaces between them. Meet the royal family who live there: the King low, the Queen high, Clara on middle C. Then read your first nine notes.
guide.new: Music is written on a staff: five lines and four spaces. Meet the royal family who live there: the King low, the Queen high, Clara on middle C. Then read your first nine notes.

guide.old: The King lives at the low end of the piano and sings low. The Queen lives at the high end and sings high. And right in the middle, on middle C, lives Clara. This chapter writes their notes down, so your eyes can read what your hands play.
guide.new: The King lives at the low end of the piano and sings low. The Queen lives at the high end and sings high. Clara lives in the middle, on middle C. Now we read their notes on paper.

guide.old: Every note lives either on a line (the line runs straight through its middle, like a skewer) or in a space: it fills the space and touches the line above and the line below, like a sandwich filling.
guide.new: On a line, the line runs through the note's middle, like a skewer. In a space, the note touches the lines above and below, like a sandwich filling.

guide.old: From a line to the very next space is a step: the next letter, the next white key. From a line to the next line, or a space to the next space, is a skip: one letter jumped over, the same skip as in the musical alphabet. Both work going up and coming down.
guide.new: Line to the next space is a step: the next letter, the next white key. Line to the next line, or space to the next space, is a skip: one letter jumped over, as in the musical alphabet. Both go up and down.

guide.old: The curly sign is the treble clef. Long ago it was simply a letter G, and its curl still wraps round the second line from the bottom: the Queen's house, so every note on that line is G.
guide.new: The treble clef began as a letter G. Its curl wraps the second line from the bottom: the Queen's house. Every note on that line is G.

guide.old: The Queen sings high, and usually the right hand reads her staff. From Clara's middle C up to the Queen's G is exactly five notes: C D E F G.
guide.new: The Queen sings high. The right hand usually reads her staff. Clara's middle C to the Queen's G is five notes: C D E F G.

guide.old: The bass clef began as a letter F. The King's house is the fourth line from the bottom, and the clef's two dots are his guards, one just above his line and one just below: the line between the guards is F.
guide.new: The bass clef began as a letter F. Its two dots are the King's guards, just above and below the fourth line from the bottom. That line is the King's house: every note on it is F.

guide.old: The King sings low, and usually the left hand reads his staff. From the King's F up to Clara is five notes too: F G A B C.
guide.new: The King sings low. The left hand usually reads his staff. The King's F to Clara is five notes too: F G A B C.

guide.old: Clara's middle C is written on a little ladder of its own: just under the Queen's staff when it belongs up there, just over the King's when it belongs down. Two places on paper, one key on the piano.
guide.new: Clara's middle C is written on a little ladder of its own: just under the Queen's staff, or just over the King's. Two places on paper, one key on the piano.

guide.old: The staff has five lines and four spaces, counted from the bottom up. A note sits either on a line (the line runs through its middle) or in a space (it touches the lines above and below). Each line and space is one letter of the musical alphabet.
guide.new: Five lines and four spaces, counted from the bottom. A note sits on a line (the line runs through it) or in a space (it touches the lines above and below). Each line and space is one letter of the musical alphabet.

guide.old: Middle C sits between the treble and bass staves, on a short line of its own. Written just under the treble staff or just over the bass staff, it is the same key on the piano, the one key both hands can reach.
guide.new: Middle C sits between the treble and bass staves, on a short line of its own. Under the treble staff or over the bass staff, it is the same key: the one both hands can reach.

guide.old: They can help, but start smaller: first the nine notes round middle C, read from three friendly places (the Queen's G, middle C and the King's F). And always check the clef before reading. The rhymes work better once the two clefs feel like two different places.
guide.new: They can help, but start smaller: the nine notes round middle C, read from three friendly places (the Queen's G, middle C and the King's F). Always check the clef first. The rhymes work better once the clefs feel like two different places.
